content.title: Where Is Siena University? NCAA Tournament Facts on Duke’s Opponent
content.text: Getty Siena University is in Loudonville, New York, in the Albany area, and the Saints are Duke’s first-round opponent in the 2026 NCAA Tournament. Siena’s admissions page says the school has about 3,000 students, while public college profiles place the acceptance rate at roughly 78%. Duke and Siena are set to meet Thursday in Greenville.Readers searching “Where is Siena?” are usually trying to place a school that pops up in March but is not part of the day-to-day national conversation. The reason this has more staying power than a simple map answer is that Siena actually has a real NCAA Tournament history, even if this particular draw against Duke is brutal.Where is Siena University?Siena is located in Loudonville, New York, just outside Albany in New York’s Capital Region. That is the quick answer most bracket readers want, especially if they know the name but cannot quite place the school geographically.Siena enrollment and acceptance rateSiena’s admissions materials list about 3,000 students. Public admissions profiles put the acceptance rate at around 77% to 78%. That makes Siena a much smaller school than many casual viewers probably expect when they first see the Saints show up opposite Duke on the bracket.How did Siena make the tournament?Siena made the NCAA Tournament by winning the MAAC Tournament, securing the program’s first trip to March Madness since 2010. The Saints entered the NCAA field at 23-11, giving them a clear “back for the first time in a while” angle that makes the geo query more relevant this week.Has Siena ever won an NCAA tournament game?Yes. Siena is making its seventh NCAA tournament appearance, and the program’s history includes memorable NCAA Tournament wins over Vanderbilt and Ohio State during its strong 2008-10 run. That is one of the more useful “keep reading” details in this story, because it reminds readers Siena is not just some random small-school team popping up opposite Duke.The Saints have been here before, even if it has been a long wait since their last trip in 2010. That history does not make Siena likely to pull off a huge upset against Duke, but it does give the program more March credibility than many casual viewers would assume from the bracket line alone.Siena stats and top scorersSiena is led by Gavin Doty, who is averaging 17.9 points per game, according to local coverage, and Justice Shoats is another major backcourt name to know. Doty was the MAAC Tournament MVP and gives Siena a legitimate go-to scorer, even if the gap in size and talent against Duke is obvious.Siena also plays with the kind of underdog urgency that usually shows up this time of year. The Saints do not have Duke’s depth or NBA-level talent, but they do have an experienced scorer in Doty and enough recent momentum to at least make the Blue Devils work for stretches if they shoot well early.Prediction: Can Siena upset Duke?Siena has enough history to make people remember past March surprises, but this is still asking a lot. Prediction: Duke 85, Siena 60. The more interesting part of the story is Siena’s history and how long it has been since the Saints were back on this stage.
